title: Microinteraction language and motion library for Console components and dashboards
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Define a compact, reusable microinteraction language and motion library for the Redwood Console component system. This ticket covers library definitions, Figma components/prototypes, accessibility and reduced-motion considerations, and a consistency audit across Dashboard, Rollouts, and Cost views. The outcome should be a documented motion vocabulary with concrete component tokens (duration, easing, magnitude), ready-to-use Figma components, and a handoff package for frontend engineers that includes performance budgets and implementation guidance.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Motion vocabulary defined and approved by Design + PM (durations, easings, scale, opacity ranges).

A2: Figma library updated with motion-aware variants for 12 core components (buttons, toasts, modals, dropdowns, cards, sparklines, rollout rails, budget chips, cost popovers, table row transitions, empty states, inline alerts).
A3: High-fidelity prototype demonstrating dashboard load sequence, rollout canary animation, and cost-forecast microinteractions published to the Console design space.
A4: Accessibility doc covering reduced-motion mode, motion thresholds, and testing checklist delivered.
A5: Engineering handoff artifact (token names, example CSS/JS snippets, performance budget targets) uploaded and linked in the ticket.
tasks: T1: Audit existing Console screens to catalogue current microinteractions and inconsistencies (Dashboard / Rollouts / Cost views).
T2: Draft motion vocabulary (3 duration scales: instant, short, medium, long; 4 easing presets; opacity/scale deltas) and circulate for feedback.
T3: Create Figma components with motion-aware variants and a small prototype flow for the dashboard initial render and interaction states.
T4: Write accessibility guidance for reduced-motion and add to design guidelines.
T5: Prepare engineering handoff docs: token mapping, minimal JS/ARIA patterns, and performance budget targets (max 30ms per microinteraction on p95 browsers).
T6: Run a consistency review session with PM + Eng and create follow-up tasks for components that need rework.
T7: Publish motion library in the Console Figma space and announce in #design-console.
decisions: D1: Use three core duration tiers: short 120ms, medium 240ms, long 360ms — chosen to balance perceived responsiveness and clarity on state change.
D2: Easing presets to be named: neutral, soft, spring — neutral (cubic-bezier(0.2,0.0,0.2,1)), soft (cubic-bezier(0.25,0.1,0.25,1)), spring (custom param for interactive drags).
D3: Motion tokens will be published with 'motion.' prefix in the design token registry: motion.duration.short, motion.duration.medium, motion.easing.soft, motion.opacity.delta.small, etc.
D4: Reduced-motion preference will map to a minimal fade-only pattern; scale/translate animations will be disabled. This will be part of acceptance testing.
